content.text: In countries like Zimbabwe, where conventional payment platforms are severely restricted, digital creators face significant challenges in [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/setting-up-nowpayments-webhooks-cloudflare-workers-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-stripe-alternatives-nigerian-6|COREMERCH guide to everything]]-you-10|setting]] up online stores. With Stripe and PayPal unavailable, creators must look for alternative solutions to sell their digital products and accept [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/crypto-payments-tanzanian-online-sellers-step-step-deployment-4|Crypto Payments]] payments. This is where COREMERCH comes in, offering a sovereign commerce infrastructure that empowers creators to take control of their online stores.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The COREMERCH infrastructure is designed to work around platform restrictions, providing a decentralized solution for digital creators. By leveraging GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, creators can establish a fully operational online store without relying on conventional payment platforms. This infrastructure is not a workaround, but a base-layer solution that gives creators full ownership and control over their stores.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your crypto store, you need to have a clear understanding of your product offerings, target audience, and marketing strategy. You should also have a basic understanding of crypto payments and how they work. Additionally, you will need to set up a NOWPayments account, which will enable you to accept crypto payments on your store. With these elements in place, you can begin the deployment process, which can take as little as 4-6 hours following the Sovereign Blueprint for Stack 01.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

The payment and delivery pipeline is a critical component of your crypto store. With NOWPayments, you can accept over 300 cryptocurrencies, with a low fee of 0.5% per transaction. To set up your pipeline, you will need to configure your NOWPayments account, connect it to your store, and test the payment process. You should also set up a system for delivering digital products to customers, such as Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. By streamlining your payment and delivery pipeline, you can ensure a seamless customer experience and minimize the risk of errors or disputes.
Build a sovereign commerce infrastructure that gives you full ownership and control over your online store.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your store is set up and your payment and delivery pipeline is configured, you can go live and start processing transactions. This is an exciting moment, as you will be able to see your store in action and start generating revenue. To ensure a smooth launch, you should test your store thoroughly, including the payment and delivery process. You should also have a plan in place for handling customer support and resolving any issues that may arise. With the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), you can get your store up and running in 48 hours, with end-to-end testing and 30-day support to ensure a successful launch.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your store grows and you start to generate more revenue, you will need to scale your infrastructure to meet increasing demand. This may involve upgrading your hosting plan, adding more products to your store, or expanding your marketing efforts. With the COREMERCH infrastructure, you can scale your store quickly and easily, without worrying about platform restrictions or fees. By leveraging the power of crypto payments and decentralized infrastructure, you can build a successful and sustainable online business that is not dependent on conventional payment platforms.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your crypto store, start by setting up your NOWPayments account and configuring your payment pipeline. Next, connect your payment pipeline to your store and test the payment process. Then, set up a system for delivering digital products to customers, such as Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. After that, test your store thoroughly, including the payment and delivery process. Finally, go live and start processing transactions, with a plan in place for handling customer support and resolving any issues that may arise. By following these steps, you can ensure a successful launch and start generating revenue from your online store.
